paper.title_en: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
paper.abstract_en: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.
